# `js/no-use-before-define`

**No variable, function or class used before it is defined**

| | |
|---|---|
| **Pack** | `@codelaw/rules-js` (npm) · `codelaw-rules-js` (PyPI) |
| **Languages** | JavaScript, JSX, TypeScript, TSX |
| **Turned on by** | no preset — name it in `[rules]` |
| **Severity when named without one** | `error` |
| **Options** | `functions`, `classes`, `variables`, `allowNamedExports` |
| **Fix** | `manual` — no automatic fix; the steps are under *How to fix* (moving a definition above its first use reorders the file) |
| **Stability** | `preview` — runs only with `preview = true` |
| **Since** | 0.5.0 |
| **Ported from** | `eslint/no-use-before-define` |

## What it checks

A reference that comes, in source order, before the declaration it resolves to is reported — also one inside the declarator's own value (`const a = a + 1`). With ESLint's defaults that includes hoisted functions and `var`s and references from inner functions; the `functions`, `classes`, `variables` and `allowNamedExports` options relax it as ESLint's do. TypeScript type references, interfaces and type aliases are not this rule's.

**Why:** A `let`, `const` or `class` read before its line throws; a hoisted `var` reads `undefined`; and code is easier to follow when names are defined first.

## Configuration

Everything below goes in `codelaw.toml` at the repo root. The same keys work as `[tool.codelaw]` in `pyproject.toml` or `"codelaw"` in `package.json` ([SR-CONFIG](../../../records/0110_config.md)).

### Turn it on

**Install the pack** (`codelaw init` does it for the languages it finds):

```bash
npm install --save-dev @codelaw/rules-js
pip install codelaw-rules-js
```

**No preset turns it on.** Load its pack through any preset (`codelaw:js/recommended` here), then name the rule in `[rules]`:

```toml
preview = true                        # pack rules are preview today
extends = ["codelaw:js/recommended"]

[rules]
"js/no-use-before-define" = "error"
```

- **A rule exists only once its pack is loaded** through `extends`; naming it in `[rules]` without that is an unknown rule id (exit 2).
- **Without `preview = true`** the rule is skipped and codelaw warns that it is preview.

### Severity

```toml
[rules]
"js/no-use-before-define" = "warn"    # error | warn | info | off
```

- **`error`** fails the run (exit 1) · **`warn`** fails only with `--max-warnings N` · **`info`** never fails · **`off`** turns it off.
- **Naming it with a severity turns it on** even when no preset does.

### Options

| Option | Type | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `functions` | `boolean` | `true` | report functions used before their declaration |
| `classes` | `boolean` | `true` | report classes used before their declaration from an inner function |
| `variables` | `boolean` | `true` | report variables used before their declaration from an inner function |
| `allowNamedExports` | `boolean` | `false` | allow `export { x }` above `x` |

**Every option at its default** — a starting point to copy:

```toml
[rules."js/no-use-before-define"]
severity = "error"

[rules."js/no-use-before-define".options]
functions = true
classes = true
variables = true
allowNamedExports = false
```

**The same, inline, with example values:**

```toml
[rules]
"js/no-use-before-define" = { severity = "error", options = { functions = false, classes = false, variables = false, allowNamedExports = true } }
```

- **A table without `severity`** changes only the options: the severity stays what a preset or an earlier layer set, and a rule that is off stays off.
- **A list option replaces its default** — copy the default entries you want to keep.
- **An unknown option or a value of the wrong type** stops the run with exit 2 and names the nearest option.

#### `functions`

*boolean* · default `true`

report functions used before their declaration

```toml
[rules."js/no-use-before-define".options]
functions = false
```

#### `classes`

*boolean* · default `true`

report classes used before their declaration from an inner function

```toml
[rules."js/no-use-before-define".options]
classes = false
```

#### `variables`

*boolean* · default `true`

report variables used before their declaration from an inner function

```toml
[rules."js/no-use-before-define".options]
variables = false
```

#### `allowNamedExports`

*boolean* · default `false`

allow `export { x }` above `x`

```toml
[rules."js/no-use-before-define".options]
allowNamedExports = true
```

### Options in action

Each case below is one of the rule's tests (`packs/js/rules/js/no-use-before-define.cases.md`): the options, the input, and what codelaw reports.

#### functions allowed

```toml
[rules."js/no-use-before-define".options]
functions = false
```

```js
run();
function run() {}
```

**Reports nothing.**

#### named export above

```toml
[rules."js/no-use-before-define".options]
allowNamedExports = true
```

```js
export { x };
const x = 1;
```

**Reports nothing.**

### For a group of files

A `[scope.<name>]` gives some files their own setting, applied after `[rules]` — the `tests` scope `codelaw:js/recommended` ships (`**/*.test.*`, `**/*.spec.*`); naming it extends it, so its files stay:

```toml
[scope.tests]
rules = { "js/no-use-before-define" = { options = { functions = false } } }
```

Or switch it off there:

```toml
[scope.tests]
rules = { "js/no-use-before-define" = "off" }
```

A scope's `remap` changes whole severities in its files, after everything else: `remap = { error = "warn" }` never fails the run there.

### Warn locally, fail in CI

The `ci` profile runs when `CI` is set; `local` otherwise; `--profile <name>` or `CODELAW_PROFILE` picks one.

```toml
[profile.local.rules]
"js/no-use-before-define" = "warn"

[profile.ci.rules]
"js/no-use-before-define" = "error"
```

### In `pyproject.toml` or `package.json`

```toml
# pyproject.toml
[tool.codelaw.rules]
"js/no-use-before-define" = { severity = "warn", options = { functions = false } }
```

```json
{
  "codelaw": {
    "rules": {
      "js/no-use-before-define": {"severity": "warn", "options": {"functions": false}}
    }
  }
}
```

### Silence one finding

An inline `codelaw-ignore` always needs a reason; `expires=`, `warn_days=` and `by=` date it ([SR-LINTER](../../../records/0106_linter.md) decision 6).

- **JavaScript:** `// codelaw-ignore js/no-use-before-define: <reason>`
- **Dated:** `// codelaw-ignore js/no-use-before-define expires=2026-12-31 by=you@example.com: <reason>`

### Keep today's findings, fail on new ones

```bash
codelaw baseline add --rule js/no-use-before-define --expires 2026-12-31 --reason "<why>"
```

See [SR-BASELINE](../../../records/0104_baseline-and-deprecations.md).

### See what applies

```bash
codelaw explain js/no-use-before-define       # what it wants, why, how to fix
codelaw check --rule js/no-use-before-define  # only this rule
codelaw config --print --for <file>           # the resolved setting, and where it came from
```

## How to fix

1. Move the declaration above its first use.

## Examples

### JavaScript

#### Don't

```js
greet();
const name = "x";
function greet() {
  return name;
}
```

#### Do

```js
const name = "x";
function greet() {
  return name;
}
greet();
```

### JSX

#### Don't

```jsx
greet();
const name = "x";
function greet() {
  return name;
}
```

#### Do

```jsx
const name = "x";
function greet() {
  return name;
}
greet();
```

### TypeScript

#### Don't

```ts
greet();
const name = "x";
function greet() {
  return name;
}
```

#### Do

```ts
const name = "x";
function greet() {
  return name;
}
greet();
```

### TSX

#### Don't

```tsx
greet();
const name = "x";
function greet() {
  return name;
}
```

#### Do

```tsx
const name = "x";
function greet() {
  return name;
}
greet();
```
